items.stem: When documenting an existing process, what should the SOP capture first?

options.text: How the process actually works today (as-is)
options.rationale: Correct: accurate documentation must reflect reality before any improvement.
Documenting a to-be process first can misrepresent current operations.
Tools are secondary to the actual steps.
A title does not describe the process.

items.explanation: Correct: accurate documentation must reflect reality before any improvement.

items.stem: What makes an SOP usable by a new hire?

options.text: Clear numbered steps with roles, inputs and outputs
options.rationale: Correct: explicit, self-contained steps let someone new follow it without guessing.
Assumed knowledge defeats the purpose for a new hire.
Unstructured prose is hard to follow as a procedure.

options.text: Only a flowchart with no text
options.rationale: A diagram alone often omits the detail needed to act.

items.explanation: Correct: explicit, self-contained steps let someone new follow it without guessing.

items.stem: Which TWO keep operations documentation reliable over time? (Select TWO)

options.text: Assigning an owner and a review cycle
options.rationale: Correct: ownership and scheduled review keep the document current.

options.text: Having a process owner validate accuracy
options.rationale: Correct: owner validation confirms the SOP matches reality.
Processes change, so static docs become wrong.

options.text: Keeping only an AI draft with no review

items.explanation: Correct: ownership and scheduled review keep the document current.
